rail_guard.text: Newcastle Central. The first station to be lit by electricity, nearly. Trains for every station you have visited. Mind the gap and the gannet.
All aboard! Howay, where are we off to?

ncl_geordie.text: Howay, pet! Welcome to the Toon. Geordie's not hard. 'Canny' is nice. 'Bairn' is a child. 'Hadaway' is 'oh, go on, you're having me on'.
We say 'Howay the lads'. It means 'come on, then!' Everyone says it, even to the dog.

ncl_baker.text: Greggs started right here in Newcastle, in 1939, when John Gregg started delivering eggs by bike. Now it's every high street in the land.
Howay, you'll be wanting a Greggs. The sausage roll is the national treasure, and the stottie cake is a close second. Grab a bite before you tackle the Toon.

ncl_guide.text: Seven bridges, a mile, and a river. There's the Swing Bridge, the High Level Bridge, the Tyne Bridge, the Gateshead Millennium Bridge, the Redheugh, King Edward VII and the Metro one.
The Tyne Bridge has its own colony of kittiwakes, the furthest inland in the world. In the season they are on a rota.

ncl_artstudent.text: The Baltic has no permanent collection, which is the idea. It changes every few months, so you never see the same thing twice. Unless you go to the cafe.
From the top floor you can see the whole Tyne, and the Sage, and a lot of seagulls auditioning.

ncl_freeman.text: I'm a Freeman of the City. Which gets me grazing rights on the Town Moor, among other things. I've three cows. They think they own the place, and in a way, so do I.
The Hoppings fair comes every June, the biggest travelling fair in Europe. The cows have a front row view.

ncl_busker.text: Newcastle sound? Geordie folk music. Pipes: not the Highland kind, the Northumbrian kind. Smaller, gentler, played sitting down with the bellows under the arm. Posh.
Aye, a smallpipes tune can make a grown man cry. Or a seagull. Mostly the seagull.
